versions.changelog: Shown as Transcoding Diagnostics. The page has five tabs: Hardware Probe, Recommended Settings, Performance Tests, Test Results and Help. Results can be shown as bars, values or a share of the fastest, and saved runs can be deleted. Help lists the cached test clips; clips no longer used are deleted automatically. Banners and buttons match the dashboard.
Probes and performance tests are no longer refused while a client is direct streaming (remux); only re-encoding video or audio blocks them.
Removes the hardware probe scheduled task (probing runs from the plugin page). The command-line tool's macOS and Linux builds now unpack as a runnable hwprobe. Simpler README.

Speed tab: measures transcode speed per working backend and software, for chosen inputs (test videos, film samples or a library file), codecs and player qualities, with Jellyfin's transcoding settings overridable for the run. Pause, cancel, history and a page styled like the dashboard.

Adds a diagnostics zip of the report and every ffmpeg log, downloaded from the plugin page or written by the command line with --diagnostics, to attach to a hardware report issue. Warns when Jellyfin is set to a backend that didn't work, and offers switching to software.

Tests QSV on every Intel adapter and AMF on the first AMD adapter on Windows, as Jellyfin picks them. Adds a Windows ARM64 command-line build. No longer guesses which GPU maker an unavailable option needs.
NVIDIA shows its pipeline tier (Full GPU pipeline (CUDA)). The plugin page fits phone screens.
Last change is one expandable line, listing what Revert sets each option to.
Shows what Revert would change. Asks to reload an open page after HwProbe is updated. HwProbe's API responses are no longer cached.
V4L2 says ARM devices only on x86. Results from an older HwProbe or a different ffmpeg are no longer shown; run the probe again after either changes.
Says when a backend needs another platform or GPU vendor. Only offers the HuC firmware fix to GPUs that have the encoder. Results link to their fix. Consistent fix wording.

Advice for trickplay (hardware decoding, MJPEG encoding, key frames only), enhanced NVDEC and BWDIF deinterlacing. Says when Jellyfin, not the GPU, uses software. Tests HEVC RExt in both 4:2:2 and 4:4:4. NVIDIA and V4L2 checked on real hardware.
A probe no longer starts during playback just after a client logs in again. The scheduled task no longer fails when the server is busy.
HwProbe in the dashboard sidebar. Plugin icon and catalog image.
Clearer documentation and plugin descriptions.
Says when Jellyfin can't open the GPU because of permissions, and how to fix it.
Restart button after switching backend. Test clips are downloaded or retried when they can't be made.
Apply and revert settings from the plugin page.
Reproducible builds.
First release.

name: HwProbe
description: Runs short test transcodes for each hardware acceleration option on the Transcoding and Trickplay pages. Shows which ones work, how to fix the ones that don't, and measures the performance of each. Recommended settings can be applied to Jellyfin's settings and reverted, or downloaded as a diagnostics zip to attach to an issue.
overview: Transcoding Diagnostics: tests which hardware transcoding options work on a Jellyfin server, and how fast each one transcodes
